thread:
jia: FYI saw a ~12% p95 regression on host ingress after the kernel-selection rollout last night (kern-v2). Seems concentrated around tokenization + request parse hotpath.
matt: ugh. can you paste the flamegraph or a quick perf dump? :eyes:
jia: quick dump from the perf job (prod-stable, 95thpercentile traces):
```
cpu  |  46% tokenization::{split/normalize}
cpu  |  22% request_parse::proto_unwrap
cpu  |  12% slab_io::writev
cpu  |  8% kvcache::evict_and_rehash
```
jia: p95 numbers: before roll 120ms -> after 135ms (same QPS, identical batching config). tail moved noticeably.
sam: interesting that kvcache shows up. any change in the gating heuristics or batch hints with kern-v2?
jia: kernel selection changed the vectorized UTF8 path — it reduced time inside the GPU path but added rounding to chunk boundaries which increases host-side parse churn. small writes more frequent.
matt: can you paste a minimal repro? I'd like to run locally with the same request shapes.
jia: repro (simulate 2k token prompts, 50 concurrent):
```
wrk -t50 -c50 -d30s http://ingress.local/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $$$" \
  -s ./scripts/payload_2k.json
```
leo: I saw similar symptoms on the canary earlier — microbursts of small writes forced extra syscalls. http2 write coalescing was less effective after the kernel change.
ops-bot: deploy-log: kern-v2 rolled at 2026-03-18T02:12Z to prod-stable (rev: kern-v2-20260318). No auto-revert triggered.
sam: possible mitigations: 1) enforce host-side coalescing at ingress (buffer writes until threshold), 2) tweak kernel-selection to avoid the micro-chunking for requests matching our common shapes, 3) KV cache prefetch/hint to reduce evictions.
matt: I can bisect kernel-selection knobs tomorrow. If we can add a quick sampling span on the tokenizer to measure write syscall count per request, that'll help.
jia: putting a microtrace in today. adding `host.tokenize.writev_count` and `host.parse.syscall_rate` to the route instrumentation.
sam: also check batcher heuristics: if batch packing changed its alignment, effective batch sizes might be dropping (even if nominal tokens/batch is same).
jia: noted. initial check: metrics show writev_count went up ~2x on affected routes. attaching one short log snippet:
```
[ingress] req=abc123 tokens=1984 writes=6 kvcache_hit=true parse_ms=5 token_ms=22 writev_ms=14
[ingress] req=def456 tokens=2001 writes=11 kvcache_hit=false parse_ms=8 token_ms=28 writev_ms=42
```
leo: if writes spike, http/grpc coalesce is the first defense. we can flip the small-write coalescer flag on the ingress proxy (hotpatch) and run a narrow canary.
matt: plan: 1) jia adds microtraces (today) 2) matt bisects kernel-selection knobs (tomorrow) 3) leo tries ingress coalescer toggle in canary (today afternoon) 4) sam audits kvcache gating and batch packing (EOD).
jia: I'll PR the trace and a short doc on repro steps. tagging @matt @leo for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
sam: thanks — if coalescer fix buys headroom we can avoid rolling back the kernel change. otherwise revert path is prepared. :shipit:
matt: keep updates here. I'll post bisect results in a new thread with the exact knob that flips the tail.
jia: update 3150004380 — microtraces in prod canary, writev_count confirmed up 1.9x on canary; leo is starting the coalescer toggle now.
